settings.label: Games Folder
settings.description:
The folder of MAME's ROM sets (a zip each, BIOS sets beside them)
[DEFAULT] Games/Arcade beside Local Files' Movies folder: on the OSD/OS image, on the card's OSD-OS partition

settings.label: Screen
settings.description:
How the games are listed, from the next time Arcade opens
[ORIGINAL] OSD/OS's own tree, by players, decade and maker
[ARCADE] A cabinet's selection screen: the games straight, on an arc or on a wheel, their picture, high scores and details, ◄ ► through the filters, COIN and START

settings.label: Start Filter
settings.description:
The list the Arcade screen opens on: All Games, or one of the lists, genres, players, decades and publishers Menu Filters shows
One with no games opens on All Games

settings.label: Menu Filters
settings.description:
The filters ◄ ► goes round on the Arcade screen, under their headings: the lists, the genres (Fighting, Beat 'em Up, Shmup, Run and Gun…), players, years and publishers
All Games is always there, a publisher only once turned on

settings.label: Play at Startup
settings.description:
One of your favorite games, started as OSD/OS starts, as a game's options set it too
[NONE] No game starts with OSD/OS
There is one for the whole of OSD/OS: choosing a game replaces another module's

settings.label: List Style
settings.description:
How the games lie on the Arcade screen
[STRAIGHT] One under another, a page at a time
[CURVED] On an arc, a page at a time
[3D CURVED] On a wheel: the game chosen goes up and down it, furthest out, the others going back, nearer each other and fading the further they are from it, and the wheel turns at its top and bottom rows

settings.label: Border
settings.description:
The frames round the Arcade screen's picture and the box under it
[OFF] No frames: the picture and the box stand on their ground alone

settings.label: Info Background
settings.description:
The ground under the Arcade screen's picture and the box of the game's high scores and details, over Settings' Background Effect
[TRANSPARENT] The background shows through  [SOLID] None of it

settings.label: Screen Adjustment
settings.description:
Fits the Arcade screen to your screen: a frame round it whose sides ▲ ▼ ◄ ► move out, or in after select, the list holding as many games as fit
Hold select to put it back as it was made; back keeps it

settings.label: Hint Bar
settings.description:
The key hints at the foot of the Arcade screen
[OFF] No bar: the list takes a game more, the box under the picture more of the game's details

settings.label: Help Line
settings.description:
The game's full name, as MAME has it, and those of its maker, year, players and system the box under the picture has no line for, under the Arcade screen's list
[OFF] No line: the list takes a game more, the box more of the game's details

settings.label: Start Info Screen
settings.description:
Before a game, how to come back to OSD/OS (and from the Arcade screen, the credits going in)
[OFF] The game starts straight from the list

settings.label: Save High Scores
settings.description:
Keep each game's high score table, as MAME's hiscore plugin does
For the games that forget it when they are switched off

settings.label: Online High Scores
settings.description:
High scores from the internet beside this machine's own
[RETROACHIEVEMENTS] A game FinalBurn Neo has plays in it, in hardcore mode, its scores going to RetroAchievements, and the Arcade screen shows its leaderboard's top three

settings.label: RetroAchievements Account
settings.description:
The account the scores go to with Online High Scores, and the Web API key the leaderboards, the games' pictures and their achievements are read with
With a key, the pictures RetroAchievements has of a game are downloaded as it is shown, or every game's with Read the Games Again, into the games folder's snap folder, named after it (sf2_1.png, sf2_2.png…) and never over a file there

settings.label: Online Play
settings.description:
Playing a game with someone over the internet, in FinalBurn Neo
[ON] Online Games lists the rooms RetroArch's lobby has of your games, RetroArch Lobby every room of it, Playable Online the games that can be played online, and a game's options can host one

settings.label: Relay Server
settings.description: Where a game you host is relayed from, for players a home router would turn away: the nearest plays smoothest

settings.label: LAN Play
settings.description:
Playing a game with someone on the same network, in FinalBurn Neo: straight from one machine to the other, without the internet
[ON] LAN Games lists the games hosted on the network that you have, and a game's options can host one

settings.label: Online Name
settings.description:
The name the others see, online and on the network
[DEFAULT] Online, the RetroAchievements account's, else OSD-OS; on the network, this device's name (Settings → About → System Information)

settings.label: FinalBurn Neo
settings.description: The second engine, RetroArch with the FinalBurn Neo core, for online high scores and play: what is installed, and the core's download

settings.label: Emulator Video
settings.description: How MAME and FinalBurn Neo draw a game's picture on your screen

settings.label: Screen Shape
settings.description:
Your screen's shape, which a game's picture is drawn to in its own shape
[AUTO] 4:3 on a CRT's display output (a TV, a JAMMA cabinet), whatever its pixels are; Square Pixels on HDMI  [16:9] A widescreen TV  [SQUARE PIXELS] As the screen's pixels give it

settings.label: Integer Scale
settings.description:
A game's lines drawn whole, once or twice, rather than spread over the screen's: sharp lines, with a thin border above and below
[AUTO] On a CRT's display output  [OFF] The picture fills the screen's height
A game with more lines than the screen fills it either way

settings.label: MAME Video
settings.description:
How MAME draws the game
[AUTO] As MAME's own settings say
Try another when a game shows no picture

settings.label: Read the Games Again
settings.description:
Ask MAME about every game in the folder again
With a Web API key, the pictures RetroAchievements has of every game are then downloaded too, a game a second, in the background
